verdict.headline: AI stocks lead a 1% Nasdaq gain on reported revenue, then Meta beats and keeps its spending range
verdict.label: Close: Nasdaq 26,702.86 (+1.05%), S&P 500 7,757.22 (+0.58%), Dow 52,856.09 (+0.69%), Russell 2000 ~2,781 (+0.27%); VIX 16.68; 10Y ~5.11%; Brent ~$109; Super Micro ~+10%, SpaceX ~+8% to +10%, Netflix -5.3%; Meta ~+2% to +5% after hours, Lam Research ~-5% after hours.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: the Nasdaq rose 1.05% to 26,702.86, closing above Monday's 26,430.89, as Super Micro (about +10%) and SpaceX (about +8% to +10%) extended the gains from Tuesday's after-hours results. The S&P 500 rose 0.58% and the Dow 0.69%. Seoul's Kospi rose 3.29% as Samsung and SK hynix gained more than 5%. After the close Meta reported revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26% and about $1.3 billion above estimates, guided the fourth quarter to $73-76 billion and narrowed its 2026 spending range to $135-145 billion. Lam Research fell about 5% to 6% after hours on a wide guidance range.

What it means: buyers paid for AI revenue that has been reported, the same kind of evidence that drew them to companies with reported profits on Monday and Tuesday. This morning's report said a close above 26,430.89 would show that, and it held. Rates gave no help: the 10-year eased only about a basis point to about 5.11% and Brent stayed near $109. Meta's capital spending of $34.9 billion and free cash flow of about -$2.1 billion show the funding question is being answered by revenue for now, not by cheaper building.

What would change the picture: a Nasdaq close back below 26,424.82 would show the rebound rested on two companies' results. A Brent settle above $111.99 would raise the odds of a 10-year test of 5.331% before the October 27-28 Fed meeting, while a confirmed US-Iran deal remains the clearest route below 5.0%.
verdict.lede_short: The Nasdaq rose 1.05% as Super Micro and SpaceX turned reported AI revenue into the day's biggest gains, closing above the 26,430.89 level this morning's report set as the test. After the close Meta beat on revenue and only lifted the bottom of its spending range, though its free cash flow was negative. Rates gave no help, with the 10-year near 5.11% and Brent near $109, and a Nasdaq close back below 26,424.82 would mean the rebound did not hold.

supporting_data.label: The Nasdaq rose 1.05% to 26,702.86, the S&P 500 0.58% to 7,757.22 and the Dow 0.69% to 52,856.09 — the Nasdaq led for the first time this week, reversing two sessions in which the Dow and small caps did.

Meta's third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion with capital spending of $34.9 billion and a 2026 range narrowed to $135-145 billion — revenue growth kept pace with spending this quarter, the test the market had set for it.

Super Micro raised its quarterly revenue range to $18.5-19.5 billion from $14.5-15.5 billion, against $15.23 billion expected — a 27% lift at the midpoint shows server customers ordering more, and the stock rose about 10%.

Brent traded near $109 late in the session after rising more than $2 when Iran said there were no grounds to expect progress with Washington — oil is not easing, so the rally rests on company results rather than rates.
The Kospi rose 3.29% to 5,735.66 as Samsung and SK hynix gained more than 5% — the memory makers recovered most of Tuesday's 3.73% fall before the US session opened.

Tesla's adjusted earnings of 48 cents beat estimates while net income fell 29% to $787 million and capital spending rose 110% to $4.7 billion — the beat came with lower profit as spending doubled, and the shares slipped after hours.

watchlist_mentions.note: Revenue $64.6 billion (+26%) beat by about $1.3 billion; Q4 guide $73-76 billion; Q3 capex $34.9 billion and 2026 range narrowed to $135-145 billion; free cash flow about -$2.1 billion; shares up about 2% to 5% after hours.
Up about 8% to 10% after Tuesday's results, with AI segment revenue of $7.56 billion, up 830%.
Adjusted EPS 48 cents beat on revenue of $28.05 billion, but net income fell 29% and capex rose 110% to $4.7 billion; up 3.4% in the session, about 2% to 3% lower after hours.
Down about 5% to 6% after hours on a December-quarter guide of $8.6 billion plus or minus $400 million, after a near-80% gain over a year.
Fell 5.3% after cutting its advertising forecast and guiding Q4 revenue just below estimates.

trade_setups.thesis: The index closed 272 points above Monday's 26,430.89 on reported AI revenue. Lam Research's after-hours drop tests whether the buying extends beyond the two companies that drove it.
trade_setups.entry: Monday's 26,430.89 and Tuesday's 26,424.82 below; Wednesday's 26,702.86 close above.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close back below 26,424.82 would show the rebound rested on two companies' results.

trade_setups.thesis: Revenue growth of 26% covered capital spending of $34.9 billion this quarter, but free cash flow was about -$2.1 billion and no 2027 spending figure was given.
trade_setups.entry: Wednesday's regular-session close against the after-hours gain of about 2% to 5%.
trade_setups.invalidation: The after-hours gain fading below Wednesday's close would show the market weighting cash flow over revenue.
